This appeal has been filed against the judgment and decree https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis dated 17.12.2020 passed by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, (IV Small Causes Court), Chennai, in M.C.O.P.No.2124 of 2012.

1 2.The learned counsel appearing for the appellants submitted that on 19.03.2012, at about 12.30 hours, the original claimant/ Balaji was riding the motorcycle bearing Registration No.TN-02-L-1101 at K.H.Road in front of Door No.142, Ayanavaram, Chennai.

entities.text: Prabavathi vs R.Vijayakumar on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: At that time, the lorry bearing Registration No.TN-07-AZ-7848 proceeding in the same direction came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the motorcycle, due to which, the original claimant sustained injuries.
Thereafter, the original claimant filed claim petition before the Tribunal, claiming compensation of Rs.50 Lakhs.
During the pendancy of the claim petition the said Balaji died on 28.11.2012 and his legal heirs/ appellants herein were impleaded in the claim petition.

3.The learned counsel appearing for the appellants further submitted that after adjudication, the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.22,43,888/- rounded off to Rs.22,44,000/-
with interest at the rate of 7.5% p.a. from the date of numbering of petition i.e., 30.04.2012 till the date of realization and costs
and directed the second respondent to deposit the compensation amount.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
Aggrieved by the same, the appellants claimants have filed this appeal seeking enhancement in compensation.

4.The learned counsel appearing for the appellants further submitted that the original claimant was a Railway employee and his pay certificate was marked as Ex.P11, however, P.W.3  employer of Railway's evidence is in confusion and the employer did not depose the net salary amount the original claimant took home.
Hence, this Court may set aside the impugned judgment and remand back the matter to the Tribunal to decide the net income of the original claimant by examining the employer of Railway once again.
The learned counsel further submitted that the award amount was already withdrawn by the appellants.
5.The learned counsel appearing for the second respondent Insurance Company raise no serious objection.

6.Heard the learned counsel appearing for the appellants claimants as well as the learned counsel appearing for the second respondent Insurance Company and perused the materials available on record.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

7.Considering the submission made by the learned counsel appearing for the appellants, the judgment and decree dated 17.12.2020 passed by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, (IV Small Causes Court), Chennai, in M.C.O.P.No.2124 of 2012, is set aside and the matter is remitted back to the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, (IV Small Causes Court), Chennai, for fresh adjudication only in respect of the net income of the original claimant by re-examining the employer of the Railway.

8.The civil miscellaneous appeal is allowed.
The judgment and decree dated 17.12.2020 passed by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, (IV Small Causes Court), Chennai, in M.C.O.P.No.2124 of 2012, is set aside.
